claims.title: Standard adelic character, theta and Eisenstein Fourier coefficients, and quadratic level-set densities
claims.statement: Every number field F admits a continuous standard finite-adelic additive character ψ agreeing with exp(−2πi Tr_(F/ℚ)(b)) on F; every such character has unit modulus, is trivial on Ô_F, and annihilates b Ô_F if and only if Tr_(F/ℚ)(b 𝒪_F) ⊆ ℤ. For a totally real field F of degree d = [F : ℚ], symmetric invertible matrix B of size 2M (M ≥ 3) with positive-definite majorants P_w, and Schwartz–Bruhat test φ on 𝔸_(F,f)^(2M), the orbital integral f*(φ, ·) is N Ô_F-periodic for some integer N ≥ 1, and any fundamental domain D for N 𝒪_F in ℝ^d has volume N^d |disc F|^(1/2) with character orthogonality for nonzero β ∈ N⁻¹ 𝒪_F. For the lattice indicator φ = 1_(a⁻¹ Ô_F^(2M)), integrating the averaged theta series at x + i against exp(−2πi ∑_w ρ_w(β) x_w) over D extracts vol(D) times the averaged level-β Gaussian count, whereas integrating the Eisenstein series unfolds to N^d times the product of the finite-adelic Fourier integral ∫ f*(φ, y) ψ(−β y) dλ_f(y) and the archimedean Fourier integral ∫ c_G(x + i) exp(−2πi ∑_w ρ_w(β) x_w) dx. Moreover, Fourier inversion identifies these two integrals with |disc F|^(−(M−1)) |N_(F/ℚ)(det B)|^(−1/2) D_f(β) and |N_(F/ℚ)(det B)|^(1/2) D_∞(β), where D_f ≥ 0 and D_∞ ≥ 0 are continuous densities disintegrating the finite lattice measure and archimedean Gaussian along the quadratic map u ↦ ½ uᵀ B u.
claims.hypotheses: Totally real number field F of degree d = [F : ℚ] with normalized finite-adelic additive Haar measure λ_f (λ_f(Ô_F) = 1), standard additive character ψ on 𝔸_(F,f), symmetric nonsingular 2M × 2M matrix B over F with M ≥ 3 and positive-definite real majorants P_w satisfying P_w B_w⁻¹ P_w = B_w, orthogonal probability measure space (Ω, Pr, g_f, g_∞) satisfying the ball-count hypothesis, positive integers a and N with N β ∈ 𝒪_F and N · q(a⁻¹ Ô_F^(2M)) ⊆ Ô_F, and nonzero target β ∈ F^×.
claims.correspondence: Standard-character triviality on Ô_F and compactness of quadratic values on the support of φ supply a common periodicity modulus N for f*(φ, ·) and the quadratic values. Character orthogonality on a fundamental domain D of N 𝒪_F isolates the β-level sum on the theta side, while coset decomposition over F / N 𝒪_F unfolds the Eisenstein coefficient into finite-adelic and archimedean Fourier integrals whose inversion produces continuous quadratic level-set densities D_f and D_∞.

claims.title: Coordinate Haar measures, local Gram-fibre positivity, rational lattice stability, and Euler-product factorization
claims.statement: For a CM extension E/F with conjugation σ, every 1 × 1 Hermitian matrix over E equals (β) for a unique scalar β ∈ F (nonzero when invertible). Over any local base ring R (A_∞ or F_v) with additive Haar measure λ and F-basis b of E, coordinate pullbacks define additive Haar measures on R ⊗_F E, on tuples (R ⊗_F E)^(n × M), and on Hermitian matrices Herm_n(R ⊗_F E) via the trace-diagonalization homeomorphism Herm_n(R ⊗_F E) ≃ₜ R^n × (R ⊗_F E)^(n(n−1)/2). Every local Gram-fibre measure m_S disintegrating these Haar measures is locally finite and assigns strictly positive measure to every open set meeting the regular S-fibre. The standard local coordinate lattices Λ_v ⊂ (F_v ⊗_F E)^(n × M) (generated over 𝒪_v by the basis b) are preserved at almost all finite places v by right multiplication by any invertible n × n matrix over E, left action of any matrix in GL_M(E), and block extension X ↦ diag(1, X). Consequently, for n = 0 or n + 2 ≤ M and invertible Hermitian T, any locally finite U(J, 𝔸_F)-invariant measure I supported on the T-Gram fibre factors as an Euler product with a scalar c ≥ 0, and on any restricted measurable box A_v (equal to Λ_v almost everywhere with finite local measures) with measurable archimedean test φ_∞ ≥ 0, the product ∏_v m_v(A_v) converges and ∫_(∀v, X_v ∈ A_v) φ_∞(X_∞) dI = c · (∫ φ_∞ dm_∞) · ∏_v m_v(A_v).
claims.hypotheses: CM extension E/F with conjugation σ, nondegenerate Hermitian matrix J of size M over E, F-basis b of E, standard local additive Haar measures on A_∞ and each completion F_v, associated local Gram-fibre families m_∞ and m_v, invertible n × n Hermitian matrix T over E, and locally finite U(J, 𝔸_F)-invariant Borel measure I on (𝔸_F ⊗_F E)^(n × M) supported on the T-fibre (with n = 0 or n + 2 ≤ M for the automatic local-density convergence step).
claims.correspondence: Because σ is nontrivial on a CM extension of degree two, Hermitian 1 × 1 matrices are base-field scalars and fixed elements of R ⊗_F E are recovered by half-trace, giving the coordinate Haar homeomorphism on Hermitian matrices. Local continuous congruence sections and GL_n-equivariance transport nullity across a neighborhood of regular fibres, proving strict positivity of m_S on regular open sets. Place-by-place insertion of Λ_v yields the renormalization recursion c(S) = c(S ∪ {v}) m_v(T)(Λ_v), assembling the Euler-product formula on restricted boxes.

claims.title: Cocompactness of anisotropic binary unitary quotients and Euler-product factorization up to a scalar
claims.statement: Let E/F be a CM extension and let J be an anisotropic nondegenerate 2 × 2 Hermitian matrix over E. Then the adelic unitary quotient U(J, F) ∖ U(J, 𝔸_F) is compact: there exists a compact set C ⊂ U(J, 𝔸_F) with U(J, 𝔸_F) = U(J, F) · C, and any fundamental domain 𝓕 for a Haar measure μ has finite positive covolume 0 < μ(𝓕) < ∞. Consequently, for every n ≥ 0 and every rational subset S ⊆ E^(n × 2), the normalized theta measure averaging rational-tuple counts over 𝓕 is locally finite. Combining this local finiteness with the 1 × 1 scalar identification, local finiteness of the finite Gram-fibre measures, and the quadratic-tail binary local mass estimate |m_v(β)(Λ_v) − 1| ≤ C₁ / q_v² at almost all finite places v yields, for every nonzero β ∈ F^×, a scalar c ≥ 0 such that the one-vector theta measure on the β-sphere factors as the Euler product c · (m_∞(β) ⊗ ∏_v m_v(β)).
claims.hypotheses: CM extension E/F with conjugation σ, anisotropic nondegenerate binary (M = 2) Hermitian matrix J over E, F-basis b of E, standard additive Haar measures on A_∞ and each F_v, unitary Haar measure μ and fundamental domain 𝓕 for U(J, F) in U(J, 𝔸_F), associated one-vector Gram-fibre families m_∞ and m_v, and the binary local mass bound |m_v(s)(Λ_v) − 1| ≤ C₁ / q_v² on local units s at almost all finite places v.
claims.correspondence: Anisotropy supplies a rank-zero maximal Witt frame, so unitary Siegel reduction yields a compact covering set C and finite positive covolume for U(J, F) ∖ U(J, 𝔸_F). Discreteness of rational tuples in the adelic vector space bounds every compact count uniformly by the finite number of rational tuples in C · K, giving local finiteness of the theta measure. The renormalization argument then works directly from summability of |m_v(β)(Λ_v) − 1| without needing M ≥ 3.

outstanding: The standard finite-adelic additive character, theta and Eisenstein Fourier coefficient extraction, finite and archimedean quadratic level-set densities, coordinate Haar measures, local Gram-fibre positivity, almost-everywhere lattice stability, Euler-product factorization on restricted boxes, and anisotropic binary cocompactness and scalar-factorized theta measure are reconstructed in ODN-01 through ODN-03.
